newsitem.title: MEXICO: Polls put Mexico's PRI ahead in two states.
newsitem.headline: Polls put Mexico's PRI ahead in two states.

text.p: The ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) is set to win governors' races in two northern states and has improved its showing in the mayor's race in Mexico City, according to polls published Tuesday

The surveys, carried out by Reforma newspaper's polling unit and published by the newspaper, showed the PRI moving into second place in the capital for the first time since campaigning began in earnest for the July 6 election.

The left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) continued to lead the mayor's race but its support slipped to 37 percent from 39 percent in Reforma's previous poll. The PRI rose to 22 percent from 19 percent.
That pushed the conservative National Action Party (PAN) into third place on 18 percent, down from 19 percent last time.

The poll was carried out Monday on 795 people and was the first taken since the PRI and PRD candidates, Cuauhtemoc Cardenas and Alfredo del Mazo, confronted each other in a televised debate Sunday night.
Reforma's previous survey was carried out on May 22-23, just before the debate from which the PAN candidate Carlos Castillo Peraza was excluded.
The newspaper's other surveys showed the PRI way ahead of its nearest rival the PAN in the governor's race in the northern state of San Luis Potosi, which also votes July 6.

That poll gave PRI candidate Fernando Silva Nieto 43 percent against 22 percent for the PAN's Marcelo de los Santos Fraga. Twenty-three percent did not yet know whom they would support. The survey was conducted on a sample of 825 people from May 13-17 and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent.

In the state of Queretaro to the north of Mexico City, Reforma's latest poll put the PRI's Fernando Ortiz Arana nine points clear of the PAN's Ignacio Loyola Vera in the governor's race, with 38 percent to Loyola's 29 percent.

Support for both men had risen four points since the last poll in February as the number of don't knows fell, the newspaper said. The Queretaro survey was carried out between May 17-18 on a sample of 800 people and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent.
The July 6 elections will also include a national vote for 500 congressmen and 32 senators, as well as governor's races in four other states.
